Cornelius asks Cligs about Cassian's magic, since he was sick for most of the journey to Darguun and didn't know much about it. Cligs shares what she saw and knows about Cassian's magic but more importantly, she shares her concerns that his magic is coming from an evil entity and that likely Cassian will kill them all at some point.

S.A.M. makes further conversation with Failin and convinces the man to give him the names of some House Cannith contacts he has had dealings with in the past.

docs.title: Looks like meats back on the menu...
docs.text:
On the third evening, Cassian attempts the ritual to send items to Thelanis once again, this time trying to send a pretty rock he found. As before, the ritural complets and he feels coldness in his hands and sees a swirl of frost around the rock - but it remains.

The group sets their usual wards: Cligs sets an Alarm spell and Cornelius has Snailor Swift keeping watch. In the middle of the night Snailor tries to wake Cornelius after it spots something by making him feel a wet trail across his face but he remains asleep. Eventually the creature triggers Cligs' spell and she is awoken to the sight of a giant boar. The cloud klaxon also wakes the rest of the group. Cligs attempts to put the boar to sleep so that they can deal with the situation peacefully but Cornelius has other ideas in mind - meaty ideas. The artificer attacks the board as it's under Cligs Sleep influence which interrupts the spell and angers the boar. Eventually, the group has no choice but to finish the animal off.

docs.title: 6 Olarune
docs.text: Having slaughtered the giant boar and harvested it's meat, the group re-sets their wards and heads back to bed. While the other drift off to their dreams, Cassian finds himself back in the throne room of the Forgotten Prince. He acknowledges Cassian's attempts to send him trinkets that he has found and appreciates the thought, but the ritual he taught him is intended for items that he specifically is seeking or that are special, not mundane items. With that, the Prince also gives Cassian a mission to find and send to him an item that he desires. This wasn't revealed to the rest of the group and Cassian didn't share.

docs.title: I think we need a bigger party...
docs.text:
Their remaining travels to Rose Quarry are uneventful and as their sleep was interrupted all of the group decides to use this time for a long rest. As evening begins to fall, they crest a ridge and are surprised when Failin asks them "Were you expecting company?" In the distance laid out before them is the mile long quarry and the nearby village, which strangely seems to be covered in ice despite the fact that it is quite warm. What stands out from here is a bonfire burning in the southern portion of the village and what seems like a large group of people.

The group takes time to make a more careful observation and is able to determine the following:

  • They see 4 tents, the bonfire, and two covered wagons
  • There are sixteen horses tied up nearby
  • There are 7 human shapes, wearing chainmail armor and half-faceplate as well as several skeletons in the camp
  • There is a periodic ringing sound coming from the further north side of the village, it sounds like a pick striking stone or ice.
  • They make out the emblem on the soldier's clothing, a green claw

Checking with Failin, and searching their memories, they know that these soldiers are members of the Order of the Emerald Claw - a former elite unit of knights in the Karrnath military that has since been outlawed and branded as a terrorist organization by Karrn and most other nations. They also know that many members of the organization are also followers of the Blood of Vol, the former state religion of Karrn that focuses on the divinity within each person and advocates for the use of undead.

Failin tells them that with the Emerald Claw involved he will go no further but will wait for them while they do what they need to do. He will give them 24 hours to return to this meeting spot and if they aren't back he will return to Rhukhaan Draal. The group agrees and then sets off to decide how to approach the situation in the village.

docs.title: They put the terror in terrorist
docs.text:
The plan they ultimately decide on is for Cligs and Caelin to scout out the group ahead using stealth and darkvision while S.A.M., Cornelius, and Cassian try to pose as lost adventures asking for help/their services. In their scouting, Caelin is able to determine that at least one of the humans is a Cleric of the Blood of Vol and that their are at least four skeletons, they also discover that what they thought might have been ice before is actually a 12-inch layer of glass that was molten when it covered the village and is responsible for the destruction. Cligs is able to determine that the glass is relatively new, only about 4 years old - which means it likely happened on the Day of Mourning. They both also learn about the patrolling zombie glass dwarves.

Despite this new information, the other group decides to continue on to approach the camp. As they do so, Cligs falls on her ass and alerts the camp to her presence. Two groups from the camp head out, each consisting of 2 soldiers and a skeleton, one to check on the disturbance made by Cligs and one to intercept the group of three coming their way. In the conversation that ensues between the soldiers and Cassian/S.A.M. it becomes clear that the Emerald Claw has no intention of letting them into the village, accepting their help, or in any way working with them. They also make it clear that they want them gone - now. Cassian is able to back them down from immediate violence but not to convince them of anything else, so they all retreat to regroup on a new plan.

docs.title: Taking the long way around
docs.text:
Eventually, the group settles on skirting around the village by following the edge of the quarry and going in from the north side of town. There doesn't immediately seem to be any soldiers as they make their way into town again but they do encounter more glass zombies. Caelin attempts to sneak up on of the groups and accidentally slips on the glass, alerting them to their presence. The zombies turn and take them in, but don't seem to want to attack them. This group of zombies is quickly dealt with. To test a theory, Cligs makes an illusion that taunts another pair of zombies and they immediately attack it, but when Caelin is in their view they attack anyone but them. It seems that Caelin, disguised as a soldier of the Emerald Claw, is able to avoid their detection.

With this new knowledge, Caelin scouts ahead towards the two relatively intact buildings. The first appears to be a large Cannith refinery, indicated as such by their gorgon and anvil symbol etched in the door keystone. The other is a temple of the Sovereign Host. Examining the refinery, they see one zombie that seems to be carting debris from the larger back room to the front two rooms and also hear the conversation of several soldiers. The rest of the group joins up with them and they do attempt to talk to the soldiers down but they won't hear anything of it and immediately attack. The leader of the group orders one of the soldiers to attempt to call for reinforcements while the rest dive into battle. The group successfully prevents the calling of reinforcements as well as defeats the soldiers.

docs.title: Finding the way
docs.text:
Examining the room more carefully now, they notice three large fireplaces in the North, South, and West walls made of red, white, and black stone, respectively. They also see two statues at each of the fireplaces made of the same material. In the center of the room is a large map embossed into the ground that features central Khorvaire pre-Mourning, so it shows: Aundair, Cyre, Karrnath, Thrane, and Breland. Cities, topography, and mines are clearly shown on the map but nothing is labeled. Investigating further, they find on the back of the statues the following text:

  • Red Dragon: “Whitehearth, White Seal, NE 9.”
  • Red Lion: “Tallis, Black Seal, E 4.”
  • White Wolf: “Cabblen Hall, Red Seal, SW 15.”
  • White Falcon: “Blackhearth, Black Seal, SE 12.”
  • Black Knight: “Kronu Hall, White Seal, N 6.”
  • Black Griffon: “Redhearth, Red Seal, SE 7.”

Taking this information and the map before them, Cligs tries to start at the white Cannith seal embedded in the white marble fireplace and walk 9 paces North East. This lands them in the middle of nowhere on the map. Thinking that this was likely intended for humans (actually, she was thinking that these racist humans were trying to hide information from the dwarves who lived here) and realizing that she is smol, she goes another 9 paces and see that a mine is marked. The location of Whitehearth is in a mine in the southerns hills of Cyre, roughly 30 miles east of where they are now. Using this information Cornelius works out the locations of the other locations as well:

  • Whitehearth: southern Cyre, southwest of the former town of Stillborough
  • Cabblen Hall - Southwest of Metrol, Cyre
  • Tallis - Near Sylbaran, southern Eldeen Reaches.
  • Blackhearth - near Baran's Keep, foothills of the Howling Peaks, Breland
  • Kronu Hall - King's Forest near the Brelish border with Zilargo
  • Redhearth - North of Shivairn, present day Valenar

All this information gathered, S.A.M. insists that they destroy this map and the statues to prevent others from accessing it. Cornelius opposes this, because it is a Cannith historical site, but ultimately relents. However, he and Cassian decide not to help and to go investigate the church. S.A.M., Caelin, and Cligs work to remove the statues from their bases and pile them in the center and then S.A.M. uses their massive gong to shatter the the area - making a terrible ruckus but also destroying the statues and most of the map. Separately, Cornelius and Cassian discover and excavate a chalice dedicated to Olladra in the temple.

docs.title: Gimme that blooood!
docs.text: Deciding to head out of town quickly at this point, they head back north. Blocking the road at the edge of town they find a tall, emaciated man, wearing a beautiful hooded robe of black silk embroidered with the Emerald Claw and Blood of Vol insignia. He has deathly white skin, and a thick scar runs from the corner of one gleaming red eye back past a pointed ear. He smiles, flashing sharp fangs. “What have we here?” he hisses and eyes the group with crimson eyes. Caelin immediately throws holy water at him, which Garrow is able to dodge. In the conversation that ensues he makes it clear that they can't win, he commands both the soldiers and the zombies and they are already on their way here. He wants them to surrender but they refuse. Cligs casts Sleep and at first it works; however, Caelin tries the holy water again and while it doesn't immediately seem to have the effect they were going for, it does break Garrow out of the effects of the Sleep. Garrow waves a hand at them and says "enough" and suddenly everyone but Cassian feels like he isn't a threat and is ready to leave. They start to go, Garrow lets them, and Cassian decides not to push the issue and follows his friends.

docs.title: Characters
docs.text: In your travels, you've met a number of interesting characters throughout the world. Some of them are detailed below.

docs.title: Elaydren Vown d'Cannith
docs.text:
You first meet the woman who becomes your patron at the Broken Anvil Inn, a House Gallanda run establishment in the Callestan district of Lower Dura, Sharn. She has set you on the path of recovering a number of important Cannith relics for her. At first she claims to work for Baron Jorlanna d'Cannith of Cannith West, based in Aundair. Eventually she reveals to S.A.M., in order to secure his allegiance, that she is in fact a secret operative for Merrix d'Cannith, the Baron of Cannith South.

She bears the Mark of Making is a spellcaster. Most times you've seen her she has work a dark-blue cloak.

Elaydren has a townhouse, #19, located in Parlan Tower, Middle Central, Sharn. This was the last place you saw her before she sent you to Xen'drik to hunt down Garrow and return the items he stole after attacking the townhouse.

docs.title: Lucan and Grilsha Stellos
docs.text:
Were central figures in a mission for Elaydren that took you to Zilargo and Thrane to prevent Garrow from obtaining a powerful relic, the Vampire Blade. Lucan was turned into a vampire by Calderus, the arch-vampire of Sharn, shortly after he was outed as one of their thralls by agents of the Emerald Claw. He fled the city with Grilsha providing cover and him traveling primarily in her Bag of Holding.

In Zilargo, he tried to work with an old friend and rival to secure transport to Karrnath - where he was promised a new life by a secret operative of the Emerald Claw. His contact was playing both side and while she did arrange his papers she also reported him to her handler in the Royal Eyes of Aundair and laid a trap for him. Grilsha and Lucan managed to escape and get on the Lightning Rail bound for Thrane.

Eventually, you were able to convince Lucan to give up the blade peacefully and he and Grilsha disappeared without telling you where they were going. Cligs believes there is a future love interest with Grilsha when they eventually reconnect.

docs.title: Brother Garrow
docs.text:
This priest of the Blood of Vol and commander of the Order of the Emerald Claw has been a recurring antagonist. He is also seeking the schema that Elaydren has you looking for - he has even recovered one that she didn't know the location of. He goes about in the guise of a vampire and uses his magic to enhance this image of himself. You know that he is not a vampire but is in fact a Changeling and his shapeshifting abilities have allowed him to trick you on several occasions.

Currently he is the one responsible for the attack on Elaydren's Town House and has stolen her schema, creation pattern, and notes and taken them to Xen'drik to hunt for the final piece of the puzzle. Exactly why he wants the schema is unclear but it is certain that the Emerald Claw acquiring such power can not happen and he must be stopped.

docs.title: The Lord of Blades
docs.text: The players have not encountered him directly but have run into several of his agents as they have been seeking the same objects and information. They have found and eliminated:

docs.title: Cutter, Waforged Ravager
docs.text:
• She murdered Bonal Geldem and was attempting to recover the journal he was carrying that had information on the hidden schema.
  • The party faced and defeated her atop a skybridge connecting Dalannan Tower and the Kelsa Spire, in Upper Menthis just outside Morgrave University.
  • Her final messenger was destroyed

docs.title: Glaive
docs.text:
• Glaive had been following Elaydren and then followed the party. His shifter allies heard that they were going into the sewers and so he set up an ambush for them there.
  • The party defeated him and his two feral shifter allies in the sewers below Sharn.
  • His final messenger was captured and read by S.A.M. revealing that another agent, Saber, was nearby.

docs.title: Saber
docs.text:
• He went looking for Glaive having not heard back from him and found the entrance to the sewer and followed the trail left by the players into the Ruins of Dorasharn Tower.

docs.title: Religions of Eberron
docs.text: In your travels around Eberron you have learned a bit about the various faiths of the world.

docs.title: The Sovereign Host
docs.text:
The Sovereign Host is the dominant religion of Khorvaire. Worshipers of the Sovereign Host are called Vassals and typically worship the pantheon as a whole rather than the nine deities individually. The Sovereign Host are directly related to the Dark Six, whom the Vassals believe were kicked out of the pantheon for various transgressions in an event referred to as the Schism.

Generally speaking, worship of the Host is diverse—while prominent priests and clerics exist, no central authority has sole control over the canon of beliefs. Still, some themes unite worshipers. Fundamentally, worshipers of the Host identify them as deities that govern everyday life. Prayer to the Host is contextual: a warrior seeking strength prays to Dol Dorn, while a farmer offers praise to Arawai. While most Vassals claim to wholly reject the Dark Six, some still make offerings to them.

docs.title: The Dark Six
docs.text:
The Dark Six are a pantheon of six gods cast out of the Sovereign Host. While the Sovereign Host represent positive aspects of life, the Dark Six represent aspects that people shun and fear. The Dark Six represent evil, destruction, and other insidious forces of civilization and nature, with the possible exception of the Traveler.

Most worshippers of the Sovereign Host will still offer prayers to the Dark Six, usually in the hopes of avoiding their wrath. A warrior may still offer a prayer to the Mockery to avoid betrayal, and a sailor may offer a prayer to the Devourer before leaving port. In Khorvaire, dedicated worship of the Dark Six is shunned. Those who do are usually devoted to a single god, and are often outcasts or criminals themselves. Droaam is one of the few locations where one can find open worship of the Dark Six.

docs.title: Other Faiths
docs.text: You have run into worshipers or organizations of a handful of other relgions and learned some basic information about them.

docs.title: Cults of the Dragon Below
docs.text:
The Cults of the Dragon Below are various cults that worship the dark forces of Khyber and beings from the underground realm. In modern times, cultists seek to release beings such as daelkyr, overlords, or demons or gain power from those same beings through sacrifice or devotion.Most cultists practice in secret since society at large shuns such worship.

Cults of the Dragon Below are not a unified religious doctrine. The large majority of these cultists are mad and dangerous, and they turn towards forces society shuns for personal power.

docs.title: The Blood of Vol
docs.text:
The Blood of Vol is a religion that worships the "Divinity Within" rather than an external higher power. Worshipers are known as Seekers of the Divinity Within, or simply Seekers. The religion was made the state religion of Karrnath by Kaius I at the start of the Last War, but this status was revoked by Regent Moranna.

The core doctrine of the Blood of Vol is that the promises of other faiths are simply lies—mortality is a curse inflicted by uncaring gods who jealously hoard immortality and the potential of divinity.

docs.title: The Order of the Emerald Claw
docs.text:
The Order of the Emerald Claw is an outlawed terrorist organization of Karrn patriots and Blood of Vol worshipers. Originally a military order of elite knights and necromancers in the service of the crown of Karrnath during the Last War, it has spread throughout Khorvaire and operated underground since its attempted dissolution in 976 YK. The Order continues to operate in a semi-terrorist fashion to this day, proclaiming their desire to see Karrnath once again rise to power.

While the public of Khorvaire often associate the Emerald Claw with the Blood of Vol religion, and many of its members follow the faith, the actions of the Emerald Claw are condemned by most followers of the Blood of Vol.

docs.title: Chruch of the Silver Flame
docs.text:
The Silver Flame is a force created during the Age of Demons to bind the overlords. It has a concrete purpose: it is the cage that keeps apocalyptic evil at bay. The Silver Flame is a pure force of celestial energy. It doesn't influence the world on its own, and can only empower champions who will use that gift to protect the innocent. The Flame itself doesn't speak to people; instead, it is the Voice of the Flame that guides the faithful. Ultimately, the Silver Flame is a resource; if you seek to protect the innocent from supernatural evil, you may be able to draw on the power of the Flame to aid you in your fight.

The Silver Flame protects the entire world from the evil of the overlords, and likewise, those who channel its power should protect all innocents from supernatural threats. While extremist sects may stray from this path, the core beliefs of the Church of the Silver Flame don't elevate any nation or species above another. Templars of the Silver Flame should protect everyone from evil. Friars should guide and care for all who are in need.

docs.title: Vulkoor
docs.text: The scorpion god of the Xen'drik drow tribes, his form is often depicted as a scorrow - a half-drow half-scorpion abberation. There are a number of interpretations of Vulkoor, the only ones you have encounterd are the Hunter and the Wrathful.

docs.title: Vulkoor the Hunter
docs.text: The most common interpretation of Vulkoor and favored by nomadic drow. They view Vulkoor as the ultimate crafty and fearless hunter. They worship their god by being hunters who take care of themselves. They also honor him by retelling stories of his great accomplishments, and honor him through their actions.

docs.title: Vulkoor the Wrathful
docs.text:
The drow who follow this path see him as a vengeful, merciless god responsible for disasters including the fall of the ancient giants. They seek to appease his wrath with living sacrifices, and are eager to use trespassing adventurers for this purpose. These drow tend to be less nomadic than their brethren.

Some the beliefs of his followers and imagery align with that of The Mockery, one of the Dark Six.
